newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa softens with NY to end little changed.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa softens with NY to end little changed.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures reversed early gains after New York opened and dragged prices back down toward little changed on Thursday.

July closed up a stg at 1,029 stg per tonne after edging up to a three-week high in the morning. September pared gains to one to close at 1,042. But total volume was a modest 3,410 contracts. July led volume with 964 contracts traded. Other months traded fewer than 600 contracts each.
Prices rose in the morning on light speculative buying after London and New York closed strongly on Wednesday.

A report from ED&F Man also buoyed prices early. ED&F Man cut its 1996/97 cocoa deficit forecast to between 125,000 and 150,000 tonnes from 170,000 to 230,000 previously but noted that the deficit has developed despite favourable weather in major producing countries.
It also said early settings for new West African crops was at the lowest since 1983 due to bad weather
Though traders agreed it was too early to speculate on the new crop, they said the idea of low settings lent light support.

But prices turned lower in the afternoon when New York July cocoa tried but failed to breach $1,500. When the follow-through buying from Wednesday failed to materialise, traders said speculators quickly dumped their positions.
That, coupled with light origin sales amid light volume, kept a lid on London cocoa. Ghana was said to be selling against current and new crops while the Ivory Coast sold against new crop.
But some traders remained optimistic on prices, saying summer, particularly June, was seasonally bullish for cocoa.
Technical analysts expected cocoa to inch higher in fits and starts, saying gains above stiff resistance near 1,033 would be difficult to hurdle.
They said cocoa would likely continue to trade in a range and drift higher.
